description: 20 production-ready Agent Skills for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI and OpenCode.
name: ai-agent-skills

skills.description: Use when an agent needs persistent memory across sessions, including capturing decisions and facts, compressing long notes, indexing and retrieving relevant memory at session start, deciding what to remember versus forget, and keeping a MEMORY.md file private and free of secrets.
skills.name: agent-memory

skills.description: Use when the user asks to test, debug, verify, or document a REST API. It guides the agent to probe health and core endpoints with curl, check authentication and error cases, respect rate limits, validate responses against the API contract, and save a reproducible test script so the same checks can be re-run later.
skills.name: api-tester

skills.description: Use when preparing an app for App Store or Google Play review, fixing a store rejection, writing a privacy policy or privacy manifest, choosing in-app purchase or payment flows, or auditing metadata, screenshots, and permissions before submitting a build.
skills.name: app-store-compliance

skills.description: Use when the user asks for Bangla writing, translation into Bangla, Bangla headlines, social media posts, scripts, or captions, including converting Banglish (Roman Bangla) to Bangla script and choosing formal versus casual register.
skills.name: bangla-content

skills.description: Use when training a small Bangla language model from scratch in PyTorch, including building a Bangla BPE tokenizer, pretraining a transformer, running supervised fine-tuning or LoRA, evaluating loss and perplexity, and producing a tiny CPU-runnable demo model.
skills.name: bangla-llm-train

skills.description: Use when automating a browser with an agent, filling forms, clicking through a web flow, scraping a page that needs JavaScript, taking screenshots to verify a page, or testing a web app end to end with Playwright.
skills.name: browser-automation

skills.description: Use when hunting security bugs in a codebase, API, or web application, including OWASP Top 10 issues, authentication and authorization flaws, injection, SSRF, IDOR, and leaked secrets, and when a triaged finding with severity, proof-of-concept, and a fix suggestion is needed.
skills.name: bug-hunter

skills.description: Use when reviewing a pull request, diff, or codebase for correctness, security, performance, and readability, and when actionable review comments with severity labels and concrete fixes are needed.
skills.name: code-reviewer

skills.description: Use when deploying a web app without paying for hosting, choosing between Vercel, Cloudflare Pages, GitHub Pages, and Netlify, adding a serverless API or environment variables to a free deployment, connecting a custom domain, or debugging a failed free-tier deploy.
skills.name: deploy-free

skills.description: Use when a user asks for a diagram, chart, or visual explanation of a system, process, database, or flow, including Mermaid flowcharts, sequence diagrams, ER diagrams, state diagrams, and architecture diagrams, and when an existing diagram is cluttered, unreadable, or hard to follow.
skills.name: diagram-design

skills.description: Use when the user asks for documentation: a README, user guide, API reference, tutorial, changelog, or any written explanation of code or a product. It guides the agent to write clear, structured, example-led docs with diagrams and version notes, and to keep the docs in sync with the code they describe.
skills.name: docs-writer

skills.description: Use when working on several branches at the same time, running parallel tasks or agents in one repository, switching branches without stashing or losing uncommitted work, or cleaning up extra checkouts after a merge.
skills.name: git-worktree

skills.description: Use when preparing a GitHub repository to go viral, including writing an English-first README, choosing topics, recording a demo GIF or video, writing release notes, drafting a launch post, and running a pre-publish checklist before making the repo public.
skills.name: github-viral

skills.description: Use when the user asks to verify live TV streams, IPTV playlists, or m3u8/DASH links, including checking whether a channel is live, dead, geo-blocked, or tokenized, and when cleaning up or adding channels to a playlist.
skills.name: iptv-stream-check

skills.description: Use when building an MCP (Model Context Protocol) server from scratch, adding tools, resources, or prompts to an MCP server, choosing between stdio and HTTP transport, or testing an MCP server with a client such as Claude Code, Claude Desktop, or the MCP Inspector.
skills.name: mcp-builder

skills.description: Use when running a full security audit of an application, service, or codebase, covering threat modelling, dependency and secrets checks, headers and CORS, authentication and sessions, and data exposure, and when a structured audit report with a findings table is needed.
skills.name: security-audit

skills.description: Use when the user asks for tests, test coverage, TDD, or verification that code works, including unit, integration, and end-to-end tests for Python or JavaScript/TypeScript projects, and when a bug fix or new feature needs a failing test first and a passing test after.
skills.name: test-writer

skills.description: Use when designing or reviewing a user interface, including landing pages, dashboards, forms, and mobile screens, and when an interface looks generic or AI-generated and needs specific typography, spacing, color, real content, accessibility, and mobile-first fixes.
skills.name: ui-design

skills.description: Use when downloading videos correctly, including picking the best format and quality with yt-dlp, downloading and concatenating HLS/m3u8 streams with ffmpeg, resuming interrupted downloads, and handling playlists, subtitles, and audio extraction.
skills.name: video-downloader

skills.description: Use when the user asks for research, fact-checking, comparison, or current information from the web. It guides the agent to search broadly, open primary sources, cross-check claims against at least two independent sources, cite every factual claim with a URL, and distinguish live data from stale search-index copies.
skills.name: web-research
